lines: I also built cooperating-screen for cross-device screen sharing with Flutter, WebRTC and a Node.js signaling service, aimed at real co-working with multi-user control and app-level sharing instead of plain desktop mirroring, with a browser web client and Docker-ready signaling: https://github.com/drosemann/cooperating-screen

On the satire side I built TraumaLang, my unbenchmarkable IT satire programming language written in C with no dependencies beyond libc and GCC, which compiles .tl files to C and comes with an --explain mode, a Python-to-TraumaLang rewriter and deliberately endless enterprise constructs documented as jokes rather than features: https://github.com/drosemann/TraumaLang
After over 2,000 gaming videos I made 15 videos in the Theo Browne style, archived at https://github.com/drosemann/drosemann/tree/main/theo-browne-era-video-style

-All of my domains are with netcup: d5niel.de for my portfolio, which will run on ForgeCMS (https://github.com/drosemann/forgecms) in the future, shadowunity.de for my Minecraft server, and hosting-club.de, a former hosting forum.
-For writing itself I use ed-docs, an offline-first Markdown workspace with ed/vi habits like i, a, Esc and :w: https://github.com/drosemann/ed-docs

+All of my domains are with netcup: d5niel.de for my portfolio, which will run on ForgeCMS (https://github.com/drosemann/forgecms) in the future, a Flask and MariaDB blog CMS with user accounts, a draft, scheduled, published and archived post workflow, Markdown, media uploads and Docker deployment, shadowunity.de for my Minecraft server, and hosting-club.de, a former hosting forum.

+For writing itself I use ed-docs, an offline-first Markdown workspace with ed/vi habits like i, a, Esc and :w, with no account, server or cloud sync, where documents live only in the browser's localStorage, the app shell is cached by a service worker after the first load and .md export is the backup: https://github.com/drosemann/ed-docs

Over the years every hosting era also produced a forum or blog attempt, ten in total, and I finally merged all of them into one codebase: forum-for-nerds (https://github.com/drosemann/forum-for-nerds), a self-hosted Next.js forum plus blog running on pure Docker with SQLite for dev and MariaDB in prod. Ten dead forums walked in, one nerd forum walked out.
For storage I ended up with OneDrive 365 Basic with 100 GB for 2 euros a month, after years of being convinced I'd never give Microsoft a cent, until the Windows and Samsung integration won me over.

Speed doesn't matter much to me, and if OneDrive ever offers a 500 GB cold archive tier on very slow old hard drives for one or two euros a month, I'd be the first customer, and I'd probably store all my photos there too since 100 GB is easily enough for me.
